stem: A hospital unit reviews its fall and pressure-injury rates each month as part of quality improvement. What is a primary use of these repeated measurements?

options.B: Serve only as a record-keeping requirement
options.C: Identify trends, evaluate performance, and target areas for improvement
options.D: Assign blame to an individual staff member for each event

rationale: AHRQ describes quality measures as tools for identifying quality concerns, tracking changes over time, and supporting improvement. Regular review of unit performance data can reveal trends and gaps and help teams choose or assess targeted quality-improvement efforts; it does not replace individual clinical assessment or function primarily as a punishment tool. C is correct.
educational_objective: Use longitudinal quality-measure data to identify trends and guide targeted quality improvement.
source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)
source_document_title: AHRQ Quality Indicator Tools for Data Analytics; Key Driver 2: Implement a Data-driven Quality Improvement Process
source_locator: AHRQ QIs — identify quality concerns and track changes over time; Key Driver 2 — choose QI measures and collect/review data regularly
source_claim_supported: Repeated quality measurement supports detection of quality concerns/trends, ongoing monitoring, and data-driven improvement planning.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care — quality improvement and evaluation of care outcomes
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — trend monitoring and quality improvement

source_original.stem: A hospital unit tracks its monthly fall rate and pressure injury incidence as part of ongoing quality monitoring. This data is used to:

options.A: Replacing the need for individualized client risk assessment
options.B: Having no practical application beyond record-keeping
options.C: Identifying trends and guiding targeted improvement efforts
options.D: Punishing individual staff members for any occurrence

source_original.rationale: Ongoing tracking of nurse-sensitive quality indicators such as fall rate and pressure injury incidence helps identify trends over time, evaluate the effectiveness of prevention interventions already in place, and guide targeted quality improvement efforts — a proactive, systems-level approach rather than a tool for individual staff punishment.
source_original.source_detail: Quality indicator trending is used to detect patterns, evaluate interventions, and target improvement; reviewed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Replaced the generic AHRQ homepage with exact current quality-indicator and data-driven-QI locators. Removed the unsupported claim that these particular rates necessarily evaluate a specific intervention unless the measure is explicitly linked to it.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current AHRQ QI/QI-process resources; NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: AHRQ current quality-indicator and EvidenceNOW QI pages checked 2026-08-17.
audit_findings.claim_audit: AHRQ directly supports using measures to identify concerns, track changes over time, and guide improvement.

distractor_audit.A: Unit-level QI data do not replace individual risk assessment.
distractor_audit.B: Measures are used to guide improvement, not only record keeping.
distractor_audit.C: Correct use of repeated quality data.
distractor_audit.D: QI is systems-focused rather than inherently punitive toward individuals.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: C is uniquely supported by the cited QI framework.
audit_findings.blueprint: Quality outcome evaluation fits Management of Care.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked AHRQ QI tools and Key Driver 2; C remains uniquely correct.
